data.one_liner: Client SDK for building apps on the atProtocol with end-to-end encryption.
data.what_it_does: Talks to an atSign's personal atServer to transparently handle key management, end-to-end encryption, background sync, notifications, and onboarding/APKAM enrollment. It provides platform-neutral client methods for Dart and Flutter applications.
use_when: Building a Dart CLI, server, or IoT program that connects to the atProtocol.
Handling secure peer-to-peer data synchronization and messaging through an atServer.
avoid_when: Building a Flutter web application, as Flutter web is not supported by atSign onboarding and key storage plugins.
Working with standard REST or GraphQL backends that do not use the atProtocol.
strengths: Provides end-to-end encryption and post-quantum cryptography support.
Handles complex device onboarding and APKAM enrollment natively.
weaknesses: Flutter web is not supported due to platform storage and onboarding limitations.
Requires understanding of atProtocol concepts like atSigns, atServers, and namespaces.
data.setup_notes: Requires setting up keys (such as FileAtKeysIo or device keychain), local storage backends like Hive or SQLite, and an atDirectory secondary address finder.
